transcript.text:
SailPoint ISC Personal Access Tokens use the **OAuth 2.0 client credentials** flow. The token endpoint is on your tenant's API domain.

## Request

```http
POST https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id={client_id}&client_secret={client_secret}
```

Replace `{tenant}` with your org name (e.g. `acme`).

## Examples

**curl:**
```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=${CLIENT_ID}&client_secret=${CLIENT_SECRET}"
```

**Python (requests):**
```python
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token",
    data={
        "grant_type": "client_credentials",
        "client_id": client_id,
        "client_secret": client_secret,
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()
access_token = response.json()["access_token"]
```

## Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6Ikp...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 750,
  "scope": "..."
}
```

## Using the token

Pass it as a `Bearer` token in the `Authorization` header on all subsequent API calls:

```http
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

The token expires in `expires_in` seconds (typically 750 s / ~12.5 min), so cache it and re-request before expiry.
